h1: Rwanda tourist visa from the UK
intro: Planning a holiday or a visit to family or friends in Rwanda? This page explains the Rwanda tourist visa, who needs one and what to prepare. We check the rules for your passport and apply for you.
eligibility: You are travelling for a holiday, sightseeing or to visit family or friends
You won’t work or do business during your visit
You have a return ticket and enough money for your stay

sections.heading: Do you need a Rwanda tourist visa?
sections.text: British passport holders can get a visa for Rwanda on arrival, or apply online in advance, which can make arrival quicker.

sections.heading: What a Rwanda tourist visa covers
sections.text: A Rwanda tourist visa is for holidays, sightseeing and visiting family or friends in Rwanda. It doesn't cover business meetings or paid work. If you're travelling for business, see our [Rwanda business visa](/rwanda-business-visa-uk/) page.

sections.heading: UK residents on other passports
sections.text: Rules for UK residents on other passports depend on their nationality. The East Africa Tourist Visa, which covers Rwanda, Uganda and Kenya, is also an option for some trips.

sections.heading: Rwanda tourist visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and handle Rwanda tourist visa applications for travellers across the UK, entirely online. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Rwanda.

sections.heading: Before you travel to Rwanda
sections.text:
Check the UK government’s [travel advice for Rwanda](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/rwanda) before you book, and again shortly before you go. It covers safety, local laws, health risks and the latest entry rules.

- Passport: most countries expect it to be valid for at least six months after you arrive, with blank pages for stamps. If yours is close to expiry, renew it first.
- Health: check the NHS fitfortravel website for Rwanda at least eight weeks before you travel, in case you need vaccinations or malaria tablets. Some countries ask for a yellow fever certificate if you’ve recently been somewhere with yellow fever.
- Insurance: take out travel insurance that covers medical treatment and getting you home, and check it’s valid for Rwanda.
- Bookings: carry copies of your return ticket and accommodation, as border officers can ask to see them.

We go through the entry requirements for your passport when we prepare your application, so you know exactly what to carry.

faqs.q: Can I visit family on a Rwanda tourist visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Visiting family or friends is covered by the Rwanda tourist visa.

faqs.q: Can I work in Rwanda on a Rwanda tourist visa?
faqs.a: No. Working needs a work visa or permit. Contact us and we’ll explain the options.

faqs.q: How long does a Rwanda tourist visa take?
faqs.a: Usually a few working days, but processing times vary. Apply at least a week before you travel, and earlier in busy seasons.

faqs.q: Do I need travel insurance for Rwanda?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend it. Choose a policy that covers medical treatment and repatriation, and check it’s valid for your destination before you go.
